page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.large belongs to the High Clock Speed instance family, built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 6149 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 4.0 GB of RAM, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local storage is not included, requiring external block storage for persistent data, and the baseline network bandwidth is 1 Gbps. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are absent.

Benchmark metrics demonstrate entry-level computational throughput reflective of the dual-thread single-core hardware profile. The instance records a Geekbench single-core score of 1064.0 and a multi-core score of 1258.0, placing aggregate compute capacity in lower percentile tiers across stress-ng and PassMark evaluations. Memory bandwidth reaches 10.2 GB/sec for uncached reads and 9.66 GB/sec for writes. The processor includes hardware instruction extensions such as AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2, which provide vector and cryptographic processing support, though overall parallel execution is bound by the single physical core.

Given its 1:2 compute-to-memory allocation and dedicated execution model, the instance provides predictable resource behavior without multi-tenant CPU contention. However, the absence of onboard storage and modest 1 Gbps network baseline limit throughput for data-heavy operations. Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.large is suitable for lightweight computational tasks, low-traffic web frontends, basic automation scripts, and small microservices where a low resource footprint is required.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.large is a compute-focused instance within the High Clock Speed family, utilizing KVM virtualization on x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6149 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, it features 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core with 2 threads, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory for a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no local storage and relies on external block volumes, while baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates entry-level performance, scoring 1064.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1258.0 in multi-core routines, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 10.2 GB/sec. Instruction support encompasses AVX-512F, AES, and BMI2. Given the small core count and lack of integrated storage, the instance serves lightweight background processing, entry-level web serving, minor utility workloads, and small microservices requiring dedicated compute execution.
